title: Bake-off (hos): deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
question: Who holds power in NEAR’s House of Stake? Make me a fresh flower, not an existing one.
note: A real run on NEAR AI Cloud (T060), kept with its signatures.

turns.content: I'll find the House of Stake network first.

interpretation.summary: In NEAR's House of Stake, power is veNEAR voting power: locked NEAR grown by lock time, minus delegations out plus delegations in. Voting power is extremely concentrated: the largest holder has 15.3% of all veNEAR, and five accounts together pass half. This flower orders the 60 biggest holders clockwise from the top, so the heavy end of the flower is the decision-making end of the House.

power_means.claim: Power in the House of Stake is veNEAR voting power, the contract's rule: own veNEAR minus outgoing delegations plus incoming.
Five accounts control more than half of all voting power; the top 10 hold about 81%.
Among included participants voting power is very unequal (Gini 0.976); 405 small accounts together hold 0.014% of veNEAR.

mappings.why: each account's share of veNEAR voting power, compressed into a 2x band so small holders stay visible
square root of that same share: the tallest bars are the largest voting blocs
named account ids (self-declared) versus anonymous implicit accounts, so people are not mistaken for labels
solid for self-declared names, none where no identity could be read
largest voting power first, clockwise from the top

conflicts: Delegation is a second path to power: 145 accounts delegate to 42 delegates, so delegated veNEAR can be moved and is not the same as locked NEAR.
Proposal outcome on vote.dao is another kind of power; this flower draws holdings, not votes, and per-voter votes were not read.
Governance roles from the venear.dao and vote.dao configs also carry influence, and are not drawn here.
unknowns: Addresses are not people: one person or entity may control several accounts, and common control was not determined.
Per-voter votes on the 30 vote.dao proposals were not read, so actual voting behaviour is unknown.
Each holder's lockup contract and its staking were not read, and off-chain delegate profiles were not checked.
Self-declared names are not verified identities; they are account ids only.
Petal read one final block (223162877) on 2026-11-05; later delegations or locks are not reflected.
inferred: The two largest holders use implicit (anonymous) account ids; that they are distinct actors is assumed, not proven.

**Flower:** [/draft?flower=bf1d6d7a26376329](/draft?flower=bf1d6d7a26376329)

Data: freshly read (`reused: false`), final block 223162877, as of 2026-11-05 11:58:58Z. No published flowers existed for this network, so this is new.

**What you'll see:** 60 largest veNEAR holders around the edge, largest clockwise from the top, with everyone else grouped in one hatched tail petal. Power is very concentrated: the top account holds 15.3%, five pass 50% (Nakamoto = 5), and the top 10 hold 81%.

**Mapping**
- Width & height: share of veNEAR voting power (sqrt height, width in a 2× band) — `venear-accounts`, `hos-source`
- Colour: named account id vs anonymous implicit account (self-declared, not verified) — `account-id`
- Outline: solid where a name is self-declared — `account-id`
- Order: most voting power first, clockwise — `venear-accounts`

**Changed from the default:** colour → identity (named vs anonymous).

**What this can't tell you:** addresses aren't people — several accounts may share one controller, and common control wasn't determined. Per-voter votes on the 30 vote.dao proposals weren't read, lockups and their staking weren't read, and delegation (145 accounts → 42 delegates) is a movable second path to power. Gini 0.976; 405 small accounts together hold 0.014%.
